subject: Hospitality
title: The Reservation Game
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Reservation Game usable.

hook.text: Getting a reservation at top restaurants can be harder than getting concert tickets. Some have 10,000-person waitlists.

buildup.text: OpenTable transformed reservations in 1998 by moving them online. No more busy signals—just click and book.

discovery.text: No-shows are a huge problem. Up to 20% of reservations are abandoned, wasting food, labor, and revenue.

twist.text: Restaurants now charge cancellation fees or require credit cards—treating a dinner reservation like a theater ticket.

climax.text: Apps like Resy and Tock now sell prepaid dining 'tickets,' shifting the financial risk from restaurant to diner.

punchline.text: From phone calls to prepaid tickets. Reservations became transactions.

quiz.question: Why do some restaurants now require credit cards for reservations?
options: No-shows waste up to 20% of capacity—cards reduce cancellations
